newsitem.title: ITALY: Confidence vote seen likely for Italy mini-budget.
newsitem.headline: Confidence vote seen likely for Italy mini-budget.

text.p: The Italian mini-budget is due to go back to the full lower house of parliament on May 5, with many politicians expecting the government to call a confidence vote to ram the deficit-cutting package into law.
A timetable handed out to parliamentarians on Wednesday talked of a "possible vote of confidence" for May 6.
Commentators said they thought that, if a confidence vote was called, it would be for the deficit-cutting mini-budget.

The package, which aims to cut 15.5 trillion lire off the deficit in a bid to prepare the economy for the launch of the single European currency, has to be approved by both houses of parliament before becoming law.

Parliament has to be approved by May 27. A confidence vote would brush aside opposition amendments and keep the legislation on track. Prime Minister Romano Prodi controls the Senate, but relies on the hard-left Communist Refoundation for his majority in the lower house.
